assessments:

referralPathway:
Open referral in most areas

There is no universal population screening for language
Separately, a parent, school or young person can request an EHC needs assessment
serviceModel:
Split across two systems — NHS SLT commissioned locally, schools and LAs under SEND
A mix of direct therapy, indirect work by school staff or parents, and training
A strong policy push towards the indirect and universal/targeted end
SEND Code: SLT is normally educational provision, so the LA carries it in an EHC plan
legalEntitlement:
A DLD diagnosis on its own confers no entitlement
Entitlement runs through the Children and Families Act 2014
SEN support at school level, or a statutory EHC plan (0–25) where school resources fall short

funding:
Mixed and indirect — there is no per-child DLD funding stream
NHS SLT through local NHS commissioning

workforce:
Speech and language therapists, regulated by the HCPC
The RCSLT is the professional body
Much intervention is delivered by SLT assistants, teaching assistants and teachers
Capacity relative to caseload is a long-standing pressure point
dischargeCriteria:
No national rule — set service by service
Typically episode-of-care: a block of intervention, review, then school-delivered support
Re-referral stays open
Unlike EAL status, DLD is persistent — discharge ends an episode, not the condition
outcomesEvidence:
SCALES and related longitudinal work: difficulties at school entry are highly stable

Associated with poorer attainment and more social, emotional and behavioural difficulty

legalEntitlement:
